implementation_notes: Node gives the runtime and nothing else: http.createServer(requestListener).listen(port) hands the handler a request and a writable response, so the pattern is a path comparison plus res.writeHead(200|503).end() and each check is an ordinary async function - that replaces the classic route structure without any framework. Express/Fastify reduce it to app.get('/healthz', handler), and @godaddy/terminus is the library that adds the full structure (its own description: graceful shutdown and Kubernetes readiness/liveness checks for any Node.js HTTP application) for services that prefer wiring readiness and drain over hand-rolling them. The classic registry is still justified once several checks must be aggregated with per-check timeouts and cached for the probe interval.
idiom_name: node:http request handler (or express route) + async check functions
pitfalls: An async handler that throws after the response has started leaves the probe connection hanging instead of failing: write the status and end the response deterministically on every path.

Health checks that keep timers, intervals or sockets alive prevent a graceful shutdown and leak handles across restarts - clear them in the shutdown path and expose the same state the readiness check reports.

A synchronous (CPU-bound) check blocks the single event loop that the liveness signal itself depends on, and a check without AbortSignal can outlive the orchestrator's deadline while continuing to run.
